utterances.text: I am sure you must have consulted so many people. Your client consults you, he can say, "Please do this", and you can tell him "No, do not do that." "Consultation" can be in various forms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I know what it means in English. What it means in the military context in the former Yugoslavia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I am not speaking about Serbo-Croat; I am just talking about what "consultation" can connote in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: My problem is what it means in the military context in Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time. I will pass on. Might that document be marked for identification. In your report, and again in your testimony, you stated that a Tactical Group commander could give persons who were not his subordinate orders based on orders from the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I show you another document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Incidentally, this document does not relate to Konjic, because the areas mentioned here relate to different municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The very hypothetical proposition that I was postulating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You can ask him because he knows these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You want me to pursue it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Ask him if these areas fall within the Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Does Prozor fall within the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There are some villages also mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about the villages or towns that are mentioned there -- Varva in paragraph 2 -- are they in Konjic? You may not know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot see this village of Varva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 of the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see those villages mentioned there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are no villages here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Varva, Kovacevo, and Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I think the witness may have the wrong document in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think he has been given two documents at the one time. I want you to go back to the document you said you could not read -- the Prozor document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: May we also receive a copy of this document, your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Since he could not even identify any part of it, because of illegibility, I do not think it is necessary to proceed with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If Your Honours please. I think you have another document that has been given to you in front of you, which is an order of 14 November 1992. That document is more readable, I think you will agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the back of it, there appears to be a certification, is there not -- on the back of the second page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, having regard to that certification, to the fact that it is signed, that there appears a stamp, that would satisfy all your indicia of reliability, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think just looking at the document, you would agree with me that there is no reference in it to the fact that there has been an order made by the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there is no such thing in the preamble, but based on the contents which I was able to review, I concluded that this is possible, that identical problems appeared in the majority of municipalities, that is, of the subordinate commands, so here we have an order which probably was circulated to the majority of commands, and it is a problem of poor organisation, of reconnaissance and intelligence activities, and it states that on the basis of such poor records, that new personnel be found, that they be trained to perform these reconnaissance and intelligence duties, that they also be equipped for night time reconnaissance --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is very helpful. I do not think we need read it -- we can do that but my question is more directed to those specific matters. I tender that, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have the sixth point which I want to expound. For the realisation of this order, it is the commanders of the municipal staff of defence who are responsible and it would appear that the signatory is now the superior authority to the municipal staff. He was probably copying this possibility from another document -- that they are responsible to the commanders of the municipal staff of defence, as if the person signed below is the superior authority and that is why I believe and suppose that this is a circulatory document which wanted to indicate the weakness of the intelligence service and the fact this was not contained in the preamble, I do not know, because the possibility for this is provided for that, that is, that this act be received from above and that the signatory of this document did not refer to this order in the preamble, because it when it states that day and night reconnoitring and intelligence activities are provided for, we know we had no possibility for night reconnaissance, as is the possibility in modern armies of the present day, so formally this order could not be carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us be clear, paragraph 6 is very clear -- the persons to whom the other commander should be responsible -- it is very clear. It is to no-one else other than the signatory -- that is what is stated there. Read paragraph 6 carefully, "The commanders of municipal defence headquarters shall be responsible to me for compliance with this order" -- that is what it states?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I say -- it says "we" -- "to me" -- "they are responsible to me", but he did not have under him the municipal staff and that is why I believe that we are dealing with a circulatory document sent from above so that this problem could be solved in the same way in all parts of the municipality, because he is using the plural, which are the municipal staff that can be responsible to him -- that is the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document I want to go to is document V-D/17, which appears in your language at 733 and the English version of the document is 734. It is 733 V-D/17. The document is an authorisation dated 4 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a simple question about this and it relates merely to the version of the document that appears in your language. The question I have for you on this is that there appears to be an alteration to the original document, in that a name has been taken out. Did you see the unaltered version of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any enquires as to what the name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not able to obtain an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any enquires as to who altered the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did not think that it was important, that the name was important, because it was to do with contacts with prisoners, and I did not make any enquiry into who that particular person was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to go next to V-D/53. Have you found that document? It is a list of names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of prisoners of Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you note, or did you see there that there has been an alteration or a deletion, I might call it, in 27 and 31 -- do you see in particular 31 -- I will just direct your attention to 31 -- do you see 31?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have 31.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 31 -- there is the prisoners numbered from 1 to 32, starting with Dusko Bendzo and ending with Vitomir Vlaski and immediately above 32, Vitomir Vlaski, there is a blank -- a simple question: did you ever see a version of this document with that name that appears in it -- that is number 31?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any enquires as to what that name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As this was not the subject of my enquiry, I did not make an enquiry as to which name was under that particular number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But surely you saw that it had been altered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought that it might be a technical error in the writing of the numbers. I cannot say that an alteration had taken place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in other words, you made no enquiry in relation to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I ask you to look at the document I now show you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- may I assist you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to this. I appreciate assistance but it is slowing down the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just want to say that this document was received by the witness from the Defence and this is the first time that I have seen that there is a blank space for the two names in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: My colleague --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You have already put it forward as your document. Questions can be asked about it and explanations if necessary could be made.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecutor Exhibit 225.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, have you another copy which has a correct name?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have a complete version, yes, your Honour. Brigadier, if I tell you that this was a document that was given to us by the Defence, and when we first received it, number 31 was in -- the name -- and it has now been taken out, you would not know anything about that, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender that document, your Honour. I want to move to another document, V-D/55, appearing at page 859 and the English version is 864. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I specifically want to take you to paragraph 3 of that report -- paragraph 3; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document makes reference to four attachments, which are said to be integral parts of the report. We note that three of the attachments are in your binder, but the report relating to the condition of the prisoners -- report 3 -- is not attached in your binder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not find the document and was not able to incorporate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who gave it to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If I remember, Mr. Niemann, many of these documents are documents admitted on the basis that they were relied upon for the formation of his opinion. I think that was the basis on which they were admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is just curious that the document which touches upon the condition of the prisoners, which is a fairly interesting document, is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If it was not there, he would not have considered it in making up his opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No. But if it was deliberately left out, then, in my respectful submission, I think that is a legitimate line of enquiry, to find out why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He merely relied on certain documents for the forming of his opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There may well be an innocent explanation for it, and if there is, fine, we will deal with that and move on. But if not, then I will make comments about this in my closing address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose that is the more relevant place for it -- after establishing that such a document was there, and he could not have admitted it, or he should have known about such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If I ask your Honours to draw any adverse inferences based on the fact that this document -- this annexe is not attached, the first thing I would expect the Defence to say is how unfair it is of me not to give the witness an opportunity to explain what the position is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Having established that this is a document he should have seen, and did not see, I think that sufficient background has been laid for making any other comment you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will be making adverse inferences about the fact that it was deliberately withheld, because there was an attempt not to provide your Honours with all the detail and, in particular, that this was a report which may in some respects have been damaging to the Defence and that is why they did not provide it. I will be asking your Honours to withdraw that inference. If I do not confront the witness with this, I imagine someone from the Defence would be very quick to tell us how unfair that would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If I understand him, he has not seen that document at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That may be so. I want to ask him what he did when he discovered it was not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can ask him what he did, having not seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you did not see this, what did you do about it, this annexe 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know -- I did not ask what I was to do. I saw just the other things that were given me, I did not see that particular document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I got it from the Defence, or I do not quite recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to go to another document, if I could, and that is VI-3 and it is a table or "organogram", I think it is called. 893 is the version in your language, 894 is the version in the English language. Do you have that? Did you obtain this document yourself, or was it given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was drawn up by Brigadier Mustafa Polutak, the first commander of the Tactical Group number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not ask you that, I asked you who gave it to you -- did he give it to you or did you receive it from some other third party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was given it by the municipal staff and it was drawn up by the commander of the Tactical Group, as I say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know if the document that appears there is exactly as it was authored by Mr. Polutak, or has it been altered in some way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was drawn up -- was authored by Mustafa Polutak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has it in any way been altered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know in what sense it would be altered. The essential points are that it speaks of the composition of the Tactical Group and the forces who remain on the locality of the municipality. That is the essence of the document and nothing was changed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I would ask you to look at this document, if you would, for me. We will have to put it on the overhead projector, because --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecutor document 226.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the overhead projector. That is the document that appears in your language. Do you see in the second box, which, in English, is Tactical Group 1 -- do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the version that you have in your binder there, is there anything else contained in that box -- any other words appearing in that box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It also says Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going down to the bottom on the bottom left-hand side, do you see where it says "Author: Mustafa Polutak"? Do you see the signature -- there is no signature there, you will agree with me, will you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the document that you originally had in your report, did it have a reference in the box to Konjic and did the signature of Mr. Polutak appear there -- his actual signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps I will ask it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I say, just to avoid any misunderstanding, the expert witness sent us his complete expert report, which we then said to the Prosecutor and in the box which states "Tactical Group 1", it did state "Konjic" and the document had the original signature of Brigadier Polutak. When the expert came here, he told us that, through a technical error, the box included "Konjic" and that this was not in the original document and we informed the Prosecutor of that typing error, and that is why we have an amended version here, and the Prosecutor alone has the original document with Polutak's signature and our letter informing him that Brigadier Polutak was informed of this error in the typing of the table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, did this type of exchange occur between you and the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It certainly did. The point I am endeavouring to make by this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Why then are you pressing it? If you knew so much about why there should be that difference --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Two reasons. First, it is a document the Defence are putting forward to your Honours which contains a statement of somebody else, which has been altered -- altered not by the author of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: But they informed you about the alteration.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It was altered by the Defence. They gave us the amendment without any explanation whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That is not how I understood Mr.s Residovic's explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps your Honours might like to read the letter, because I have it here. The point is that this is a document that has been amended by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: With regard to the signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Not the author -- and the signature has been taken off -- the signature and the reference to Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Who now has the original which contains the signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Can we have the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We have a copy of the original. I have just given it to the witness, your Honour. I assume the very original document is with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There are two originals?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You said "very original".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It may well be I am the only one with the original. That document contains the signature, does it not, and contains the word "Konjic" in the box?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that this amendment was made to this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As the Defence said, there was an error here with the word "Konjic". There were no other relevant errors to verify this document -- it was only the word "Konjic", and we are dealing with the composition of the Tactical Group, and those who drew up the document only had that one mistake, "Konjic". The composition of the group is correct, the composition of the forces remaining under the command of the municipal staff is correct, so no other relevant data was changed. The composition of the forces correspond in full to the actual situation. We are only dealing with one word and that is "Konjic" and Mr. Polutak, when he signed the document, did not see this. He knew that he drew up the document and did not pay attention to the word "Konjic".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you not draw everyone's attention to that in the course of your evidence, that the document had been amended from the original one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I gave it to the Defence. I do not know who the Defence gave the documents out to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we were led to believe that this was a document that was drawn up by Mr. Polutak and something that you relied upon, whereas in fact it is a document that had been amended or altered -- not by Mr. Polutak himself. That is true, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There have been no alterations here. We are quite simply dealing with the deletion of the word "Konjic". Everything else is authentic and correct, as it is in the version given previously, which means the composition of the Tactical Group, the composition of the forces within the Tactical Group, the composition of the forces of the municipal command -- so, the only difference is the word "Konjic" and that is the error of the person who copied the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I thought you were telling us earlier how important signatures were. We see the signature has been removed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually, the emphasis has been laid -- it is understood that it is something different from what should have been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases. Your Honours, I am just endeavouring to ascertain how much longer I will be. I will not be much longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If we can help it, this witness should not stay beyond today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will try to move along as expeditiously as possible and see if I can complete it. I just want you to go now for a moment --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, after this very exhaustive cross-examination, we shall be having some questions -- re-cross-examination. I do not know whether we can keep the witness for such a long time. You have already said that the visa can be extended, and we have extended it, so perhaps we can devote an hour on Tuesday morning for the continuation of this cross-examination, because I feel it to be important.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am certainly in agreement with that. I understand that it must be very difficult for the Brigadier to be here all day under this cross-examination and I think it would be a good idea if I completed my cross-examination as expeditiously as I can on Monday. I do not think I have much longer to go. I have a few more documents that I wish to show him and some general questions and that should be the end of my cross-examination. So, rather than continue on now, if he can come back next Tuesday, then certainly I would join with the Defence in suggesting that that would be an appropriate course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is it likely you will exceed 6pm?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I can try and do it by 6 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That should be enough and then on Tuesday he can just be re-examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Brigadier, would you go, please, for me to document V-D/31? Do you have that document there? This is an order from Esad Ramic dated 3 August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see there above the date, 3 August 1992, a reference to a number -- can you see that number there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that number a unique number in the sense that -- is there a separate number given on every occasion to documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know -- I do not know about protocol as regards documents. I was not interested in that subject. They are details which I did not study.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Move on then to document V-D/41.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have just received information from my client that, if he may be allowed to leave the Chamber for five minutes without interrupting the proceedings -- he has to go to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He may do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was the Tactical Group considered part of the army supreme command headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Tactical Group was not part of the supreme command -- the supreme command -- it is the Tactical Group -- the Tactical Group is a unit which is a subordinate -- it is not part of the supreme command. The supreme command is a command composition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the heading that appears there in that order immediately above "I hereby order", does that not imply -- the heading right at the top, "Army Supreme Command Headquarters, Sarajevo, Tactical Group 1" -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that not imply that the Tactical Group was considered as part of the supreme headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a confirmation of the lack of knowledge on the part of our officers. It was never part of the supreme command -- that is a lack of ignorance -- that is ignorance. What should be stated there is its formational title and in the preamble, you can relate to the order of the supreme command. It is obvious that this individual was not trained and did not have the knowledge of how to draw up a document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you would agree with me that persons who are part of the staff of Tactical Group 1 were subordinate to the commander of Tactical Group 1 -- that is an obvious situation, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course they were subordinate. First of all his command and then all the commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that, in this order, the commander of Tactical Group 1 is ordering that an offensive combat action be taken in the area as part of the "Jug" or "South" Operation and that that order is directed to Mr. Ramic -- you see paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is clear. Once again, it is an order which the commander of the Tactical Group has received from the supreme command headquarters, and in the preamble he says, "On the basis of the command of the supreme command" and then goes on to order the orders that he does, which means that in this case, in order to facilitate operations, it is necessary to engage forces in another direction, and he is transmitting what the supreme command has ordered him to do, so he is not commanding and ordering in his own personal name but following orders from the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You agree with me then that the order indicates that some of the Territorial Defence troops will participate in the "Jug" or "South" Operation and remain under the immediate authority of the Territorial Defence, with the superior authority being under the Tactical Group commander of Jug -- you will agree with that, will you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the Tactical Group Jug led the forces under his command, and here they are ordering special forces of the municipal headquarters of Konjic to use its forces in another direction to facilitate the Jug Operation, so they are not forces which entered into the composition of Operation Jug.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated in your opinion that the supreme command would decide what troops would be part of the Tactical Group, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By order of the supreme command, and that order regulates this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your opinion, since only the supreme command was superior to the municipal headquarters, only the supreme command would have the authority to determine what troops would be sent to TG1 -- that would be the position, would it not, according to your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. What we are dealing with here is that most probably the supreme command headquarters had no links with the headquarters at Konjic, but that this was done within the frameworks of the operation, that an order be given of this kind to engage the troops of the municipal forces of Konjic, in a certain locality, to help the main forces in Operation Jug.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me, would you not, that it is unusual not to provide a full description of the troops that were to be included?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Included in Operation South, do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, included in the territorial group -- the Tactical Group, I apologise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Tactical Group, when it was first set up, compositions entering into the Tactical Group must be included and must be precisely defined, the portions of the municipal forces which form the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this did not happen, did it, because the July appointment of the Tactical Group commander was not specific as to the particular troops, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was a defect in the order. He should have determined the details -- a Tactical Group was to be formed and the tasks precisely defined as well as the TG's composition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I refer to the 11 July order. I assume that if Mr. Delalic had been given authority to determine the troops that he could take from the municipal headquarters for the Tactical Group, this order would be consistent with that, and it would also show that he had superior authority over the Territorial Defence of Konjic, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The documents that I studied gave no authorisations of this kind to Zejnil Delalic, that is to say, that he could select the cadres or units which would make up the composition of the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he said that he had control over four municipalities but not all the municipalities were complete, because some parts were under the Serb control, I take it you would disagree with that, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said that this was a defect -- a weakness in that order. He cannot be given orders to form a Tactical Group from those municipalities, because the forces that he was to take for that TG were not precisely defined and the troops were not allowed to leave their positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not ask you that question, Brigadier. I was asking you a question: if he had the view that he had the responsibility, that he considered himself to have the responsibility to unify the forces from different municipalities, and hence have control over those municipalities, then you would disagree with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He could not have had any control over the municipalities -- he has no competence of that kind. His authorisation was to command the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Again, you did not answer my question. My question is: you would say you would disagree with what he said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is what his reply amounts to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Possibly, your Honours. I will pass on. Just going to document VI/11 and it appears at page 917 of your documents, and 918 -- it is an order from the commander of Tactical Group 1, Zejnil Delalic dated 28 August -- sorry, a request, 28 August 1992. Do you see that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I do not want to ask you specifically about the contents of the document. I am just asking you that this is a document that you relied on as an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, the reason why you relied on it is because of the signature, and the appearance of the stamp among other things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Excuse me, your Honours. Again, just looking at document 6/4, which appears at page 195 of your documents, and 896 and 897 is the English version -- it is 6/4 and it consists of an order from Sefer Halilovic, the chief of the armed forces main staff, appointing Zejnil Delalic -- do you see that document? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, I do not want to ask you specifically about the document, but do you see right at the very top of the document there is what appears to be the shape of a telephone, a number, and then a date and a time -- do you see that, right at the very top of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see the contents -- the protocol number is 0.2349- et cetera of 11 July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I want to go to the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: This is also a fax message.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do not believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Look at the top. It contains the seal and the signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is that very top part. You see right across the top of the document -- do you see that there? Do you see what appears to be a telephone and then a number, 384127123 right at the very top?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It goes across the page and then there is a number 23/07 -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any alterations to this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No alterations at all. This is the first time that I am paying attention to these numbers. They were not interested for me -- although it was not usual practice in documents of this kind. I do not know what those numbers in fact represent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was -- this is the document from the archives of the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I would like you to look at the document that I now show you, which is a photocopy of a Serbo-Croat version of the document or a Bosniak version of the document -- in your language. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecutor document 229.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Go to the very top again, that part we have been looking at. Do you see something that now appears in that document, which is different to the one that is in your folder?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that there are more numbers, and some letters. I do not know what the letters mean. The other number is exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. INDA-BAU -- that is the word that appears there, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have no idea who removed that reference to INDA-BAU?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what this means at all -- what the word means and whether it was in the original or not, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not asking you what it means. I am merely asking you whether you knew anything about the circumstances of how that name INDA-BAU came to be removed -- that is all I am asking you, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know nothing about this at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the archives of the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did go to the archives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, when you obtained documents from the archives of the supreme command, did you note them or mark them in any way to indicate their source?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have the source of the documents which have been authenticated -- confirmed source.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that somewhere in your papers -- is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in relation to this particular document, you could check those papers over the next few days and tell us where you received it and confirm where you received it from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I shall try to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We are nearly finished. Who had authority to determine who would be members of the command staff of the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That cannot be seen from these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not asking you about that specific one. I am just asking you a general question -- I have moved on. I am asking you who had the authority to determine who would be members of the command staff of the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say that, according to the same principle that the operative group was determined, so also was the command staff for the Tactical Group determined, if it is not indicated in the document that the commander selected his cadres himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was part of the command staff of the Tactical Group 1 during the time that Mr. Delalic was its commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know his commander, Major Pilica Sucro. I do not know the other cadres, the composition of the command, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you saying that, in your opinion, the supreme command would determine the staff of the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness has answered the question. He said that it would be normal unless there were special orders for him to be able to form the command -- the answer was given in full and in precise detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is that your answer to his question? It is for you to answer -- not your counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said that, if there was no special order regulating, then he can select the composition -- if the cadres of the group were regulated, then it can be selected by the superior authority. If he was given the order to be able to select his cadres himself, then that is another matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps you might be shown Exhibit 193, and this document that I show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Niemann, we might have to stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will be very short on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If I knew you would have exceeded 6 o'clock, we would have waited until Tuesday -- it would not have made much of a difference -- instead of getting somewhere and continuing on Tuesday. So, the Trial Chamber will now rise and we will reassemble on Tuesday at 10am.
